question: An electromagnetic radiation has frequency $6 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}$. Calculate its wavelength in free space and identify the region of the electromagnetic spectrum to which it belongs. Take $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

options.A: $\lambda = c\nu = (3 \times 10^8)(6 \times 10^{14}) = 1.8 \times 10^{23}\text{ m}$; it is a radio wave.
options.B: $\lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{6 \times 10^{14}} = 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 500\text{ nm}$; it lies in the visible region.
options.C: $\lambda = \frac{\nu}{c} = \frac{6 \times 10^{14}}{3 \times 10^8} = 2 \times 10^6\text{ m}$; it lies in the microwave region.
options.D: $\lambda = 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$; it lies in the X-ray region.
